texts.title: Package held for customs processing fee
texts.summary: A delivery service claims your package is on hold until you pay a small fee online.
texts.situation: You are waiting for an online order to arrive when a text pops up on your phone regarding a shipment.

messages.text: SwiftShip: Your delivery is on hold due to unpaid customs duty of $2.99. Pay immediately to avoid return to sender.

indicators.title: Unexpected small fee
indicators.detail: Couriers rarely ask for random digital payments via text message for customs duties.

indicators.title: False urgency
indicators.detail: Scammers create panic by demanding instant action so you do not pause to think.

indicators.title: Unfamiliar web address
indicators.detail: The URL uses an unofficial domain instead of the official courier's verified website.

texts.explanation: This is a delivery phishing scam. Scammers send mass texts about held packages, hoping you will click the link and enter your credit card details or personal information on a fake payment page.
texts.nextTime: Never click links in delivery texts. Instead, go directly to the official courier website and type in your tracking number manually.

texts.title: Unrecognized transfer flagged on your debit card
texts.summary: Claims a large transfer was attempted and asks you to click a link to cancel it.
texts.situation: You are sitting at your desk when your phone buzzes with an urgent alert about your primary checking account.

messages.text: Apex Trust Alert: We blocked a suspicious $480.00 transfer from your account to CryptoExchange. If you did not authorize this, verify your identity immediately.

indicators.title: Manufactured panic
indicators.detail: Scammers use a specific, distressing dollar amount to shock you into acting quickly without thinking.

indicators.title: Urgent call to action
indicators.detail: Legitimate banks will freeze a card for safety but will never demand immediate online verification through a text link.

indicators.title: Unfamiliar look-alike domain

texts.nextTime: Never click links in fraud alert texts. Instead, open your banking app directly or call the official customer service number listed on the back of your debit card.
